stem:
Meena's school in Nagpur runs a measles vaccination camp for all children in Class 8. The health worker explains that vaccinated children are very unlikely to become seriously ill with measles.

How does vaccination reduce serious measles infections and their spread in the school?

options.text: It cures measles in children who are already sick, so they stop spreading it.
It prepares the immune system to fight the measles virus before exposure, so fewer children fall ill and pass it on.
It kills all the measles viruses present in the classroom air.
It replaces the need for the immune system to respond to the virus.

teacher.key_rationale: Vaccines prime the immune system in advance of exposure, so vaccinated children are protected from serious illness and onward transmission is reduced. Option A is the trap for students who think vaccines are medicines taken after illness; C and D misdescribe the mechanism.
